CONCLUSIONS A novel manufacturing process was developed to fabricate metal polymer composites by additively manufacturing a metal lattice design and tailored polymer preform followed by compression overmolding of polymer composite onto the metal lattice. The obtained hybrid structures exhibited strong mechanical interlocking without the use of any bonding agents or surface treatments. The average tensile strength of these metal-polymer composites was measured experimentally as 76.4 MPa, which is 2-3x higher than the metal-polymer bonds obtained through other joining processes such as chemical etching or integrated metal-polymer AM processes. The flowability of 40 wt% CF/PA66 polymer composite into metal lattices of different heights were also experimentally analyzed and found that the polymer penetrates entirely for 4 mm thick lattice but not in the case of 13 mm thick lattice. Next, a numerical model was developed for hybrid structures, and it showed good correlation with the experiments by predicting the modulus within 20% deviation and high stress failure region. Investigation on fracture morphology of the hybrid structures using stereomicroscopy revealed that the failure occurred due to crack propagation along the interfaces and metal strut failure at the high stress neck region. Overall, the presented manufacturing process enables the fabrication of metal polymer composites with tunable mechanical properties. It opens avenues for combining custom metal lattice designs with tailored preforms to create lightweight, high- performance hybrid structures such as with local metallic reinforcements for targeted applications. Enhancing load-carrying capacity by designing metal lattices and creating continuous channels of polymer composites, choosing appropriate fiber-reinforced composites and their deposition patterns, and injection molding polymer composite into metallic lattice are part of our on-going work. 10.
